title: How to Reduce Your Cold Email Bounce Rate
metaTitle: How to Reduce Cold Email Bounce Rate (2026)
metaDescription: Why cold emails bounce, how to validate addresses before you ever hit send, and why strict gateways like Proofpoint and Cisco Ironport inflate your numbers.
excerpt: A bounce rate above 2 to 3 percent tells mailbox providers your data is dirty. Most of that number traces back to two fixable sources: addresses you never validated, and strict secure email gateways.
contentHtml:
Bounce rate is simply the share of your emails that never get delivered. It matters for more than the wasted send — a high bounce rate is one of the clearest signals a mailbox provider has that your list is dirty, and dirty lists are a hallmark of spam operations.

The working number to hold yourself to: stay under 2 percent. Cross 3 percent and you're actively damaging your sender reputation with every campaign you run. The upside is that most bounces trace back to two sources you can fix before a single email goes out.

What bounce rate actually measures

A bounce is simply a message the receiving side refused to deliver. Your sending tool logs it, and your bounce rate is bounces divided by total sends, either for one campaign or one mailbox.

It functions as a behavior signal. Google and Microsoft watch it closely because legitimate senders email people who actually exist, while spammers blast scraped or stale lists riddled with dead addresses. As your bounce rate climbs, you start looking more like the second group in the provider's eyes, no matter how good your actual intentions are.

Hard bounces vs soft bounces

Bounces aren't all the same, and the type tells you exactly what needs fixing.

  • Hard bounces are permanent — the address doesn't exist, the domain doesn't exist, or the mailbox has been closed. These are pure list-quality failures and they cause the most reputation damage by far.
  • Soft bounces are temporary — a full mailbox, a server that's briefly down, or a deferred message. A handful of these is completely normal. A pattern of them repeating on the same domain usually points to filtering, not an actual outage.

Go after hard bounces first — they're almost entirely preventable.

What actually causes bounces

Cold email bounces generally trace back to a handful of causes:

  • Invalid or stale addresses. People switch jobs, companies shut down, typos slip in. Every list decays as time passes.
  • Catch-all uncertainty. Some domains accept mail sent to literally any address, so a basic check can't tell you whether a specific mailbox is real.
  • Spam traps. Dead addresses deliberately recycled to catch senders working from scraped lists. Hitting one is a serious hit to your reputation.
  • Strict secure email gateways. The cause most people never think to check. Even a completely valid address can sit behind an aggressive gateway that refuses the message outright.

Validate before you send

The single most effective fix is validating every address before it ever reaches a live campaign. A good validator checks the format, confirms the domain can receive mail, probes the mailbox where it can, and then sorts each address into deliverable, risky, or undeliverable.

Drop the undeliverable ones outright and think carefully before including the risky ones. Sendbox runs email validation automatically on import, so bad addresses get flagged before they can ever reach a campaign, and the free email verifier is there for spot-checking individual addresses. Validation alone typically takes a painful bounce rate down to a safe one.

The gateway problem nobody warns you about

A Secure Email Gateway, or SEG, is a filtering layer sitting in front of a company's inboxes, screening everything that comes in. Proofpoint, Cisco Ironport, Mimecast, and Barracuda are the names you'll run into most, and all of them are designed to be strict by default.

Here's why they wreak havoc on your bounce rate. The recipient's address is perfectly valid, but the gateway in front of it aggressively refuses or quarantines cold email before it ever reaches the actual person. Depending on which gateway it is, that shows up either as a straight bounce or as a silent quarantine that still drags down your engagement numbers. Either way, sending blind into SEG-protected domains inflates both your bounce rate and complaint rate with addresses that were never going to convert regardless. Enterprise domains are especially likely to run one of these.

Working around strict gateways

You can't validate your way past a SEG, because technically the address really is valid. The fix is catching the gateway before you send and deciding your move in advance.

Sendbox has SEG detection built in. Before a campaign goes out, it checks whether each recipient's domain sits behind a Secure Email Gateway. From there you choose: skip those leads entirely so they never touch your campaign metrics, or route them through mailboxes you've specifically designated for SEG handling. Most cold email tools send blind and leave you to reverse-engineer why deliverability tanked afterward. Catching the gateway upfront keeps bounce and spam rates on your main mailboxes clean, protecting the dedicated IP reputation you spent weeks building.

Watch it per mailbox

Bounce rate isn't something you check once and forget. Track it continuously, and track it per mailbox rather than just per campaign. A campaign-wide average sitting at 2 percent can easily be hiding one mailbox running at 8 percent while the rest stay clean.

Sendbox surfaces bounce rate per mailbox in real time alongside reply rate, so a struggling mailbox stands out before the damage has a chance to spread. When one does slip, pull it from active campaigns and run warmup to rebuild it. The free bounce rate calculator is a quick way to sanity-check how a campaign landed.

Put it all together and the playbook is simple: validate every address, catch and route around SEGs before sending, and keep an eye on bounce rate per mailbox so nothing sneaks up on you. Handle those three things and bounce rate stops being a threat to your reputation. For the bigger picture, the deliverability guide covers every other lever, and the fix-it playbook covers what to do once your numbers have already gone bad.

faqs.question: What is a good bounce rate for cold email?
faqs.answer: Stay under 2 percent. Between 2 and 3 percent deserves attention, and past 3 percent you're actively damaging your sender reputation with every send. A well-validated list sent from a healthy setup should sit comfortably below 2 percent.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a hard bounce and a soft bounce?
faqs.answer: A hard bounce is permanent — the address or domain doesn't exist, or the mailbox has been closed. A soft bounce is temporary — a full mailbox, a brief server hiccup, or a deferral. Hard bounces do far more reputation damage and are almost entirely preventable through validation.

faqs.question: What is a Secure Email Gateway and why does it cause bounces?
faqs.answer: A Secure Email Gateway — Proofpoint, Cisco Ironport, Mimecast, or Barracuda are the common ones — is a strict filtering layer sitting in front of a company's inboxes. Even when the recipient's address is valid, the gateway can refuse or quarantine cold email before it ever reaches the person, inflating both your bounce rate and complaint rate.

faqs.question: Should I skip SEG-protected leads entirely?
faqs.answer: Often, yes, especially early on, since SEG-protected domains carry more bounce and spam risk for relatively little upside. The alternative is routing them through mailboxes set aside specifically for SEG handling, keeping the risk off your main sending. Sendbox's SEG detection lets you do either.

faqs.question: How do I lower my bounce rate before a campaign?
faqs.answer: Validate every address and cut the undeliverable ones, identify SEG-protected domains and either skip or route them separately, and never send to a list you haven't cleaned first. Validation and SEG detection together eliminate the two biggest sources of bounces before a single email leaves your account.

faqs.question: Does a high bounce rate affect my future campaigns?
faqs.answer: Yes. Bounce rate feeds directly into your sender reputation, and a damaged reputation carries forward into everything you send afterward. One campaign to a dirty or SEG-heavy list can suppress deliverability for weeks, which is exactly why prevention through validation and SEG detection matters more than any fix applied after the fact.
